definition: Relapse prevention is the use of approaches intended to lower the chance that major depressive disorder will return after improvement. In this context, cognitive behavioral therapy and related forms are discussed as possible ways to reduce relapse.

reasons: The packet only supports a disease-specific context: CBT and its modifications might be effective for reducing relapse of major depressive disorder. It does not support defining relapse prevention generally as any approaches intended to lower the chance a disorder will return after improvement.
The wording goes beyond the source by presenting relapse prevention as a settled functional definition, while the packet is limited to a review's aim and a tentative claim ('might be effective').

The definition states relapse prevention refers to lowering the chance that major depressive disorder will return after improvement; the packet only mentions relapse risk and relapse of MDD, and does not support the “after improvement” framing.

The definition’s general description (“use of approaches intended to lower the chance…”) is not explicitly supported by the packet text provided, which only states that CBT and its modifications “might be effective” for relapse prevention and that the review aimed to reduce relapse.
